# CUDA-Q parity matrix

This scoreboard is generated from `contracts/cudaq-parity-matrix.toml`. It compares the CUDA-Q capability baseline against FlagQuantum. FlagQuantum maturity levels, owners, limitations, and evidence paths are read from `capability-maturity.toml` and are not restated here; a row whose registry column reads `none` has no registered maturity entry.

- CUDA-Q baseline versions: 0.15.1, 0.16.0.post1
- Pinned component: CUDA-Q core
- Baseline component: cudaq-qec, also shipped as libs/qec inside NVIDIA/cudaqx
- Component release line: 0.1.0, 0.2.0, 0.2.1, 0.3.0, 0.4.0, 0.4.0.post1, 0.5.0, 0.5.0.post1, 0.6.0, 0.7.0, 0.8.0
- Component version the `quantum_error_correction` rows were read at: 0.8.0
- Component release index: https://pypi.org/pypi/cudaq-qec/json

The top-level cudaq_versions pin describes CUDA-Q core, which is the product both the export contract and this matrix describe. The QEC component ships on its own release line, so a quantum_error_correction row is only as strong as the component version it was read at, and this table records that version separately rather than implying that the pin reaches it. The tool fails closed in both directions: a pin that overlaps the component release line needs a mapping entry, and a mapping entry across two lines that do not overlap is refused as a correspondence nothing supports.

Provenance limit: No cudaq-qec release maps to either pinned CUDA-Q version: the component's release line runs from 0.1.0 to 0.8.0 while the pin is 0.15.1 and 0.16.0.post1, and the two lines are disjoint. Every quantum_error_correction row therefore records the component surface as it stands at 0.8.0. That the same surface exists at the pinned CUDA-Q baseline is not established by this contract, so a QEC row must not be read as a statement about CUDA-Q 0.15.1 or 0.16.0.post1, and a row that needs to be is a new capture rather than a new reading.
- Baseline survey: `docs/development/CUDAQ_PARITY_BASELINE.md`
- Capture method: documented_capability_survey_with_probes
- Scope: CUDA-Q capabilities observable from the public Python API, the documented backend roster, and the shipped repository tree of the pinned versions.

Baseline probes:

A probe is a runnable repository script whose JSON payload can be landed as evidence. `runnable` means the probe starts and emits its schema. `measured` means a payload from a named machine is landed under benchmarks/results with the source revision, container image, environment, and methodology recorded next to it, and that benchmarks/audit_results.py accepts it. Every probe must declare a versioned schema identifier and a source identity.

| Probe | Status | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `benchmarks/cudaq_gradient_capability_probe.py` | measured | Which gradient strategies the installed CUDA-Q exposes through cudaq.gradients, by runtime public-symbol inspection. |
| `benchmarks/cudaq_backend_compare.py` | measured | Wall-clock and precision comparison of one FlagQuantum JAX kernel against one CUDA-Q target on a matched circuit, observable, dtype, gradient method, warmup, and iteration count. |

First capture, `benchmarks/cudaq_gradient_capability_probe.py`: CUDA-Q 0.16.0.post1 exported ParameterShift, CentralDifference, ForwardDifference, and gradient, and exposed no adjoint, reverse, or backprop symbol. On 2026-09-30 the same survey ran three times on each of jp-a800-172 and jp-a800-171, against cuda-quantum-cu12 and cuda-quantum-cu13 respectively, and returned a byte-identical capability record on both hosts, so the statement is a property of the release rather than of one installed wheel.

Landed payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/cudaq_gradient_capability_a800_20260930.json`

Reading of that payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/CUDAQ_BACKEND_COMPARE_A800_20260930.md`

First capture, `benchmarks/cudaq_backend_compare.py`: On 2026-09-30 on jp-a800-172 and jp-a800-171, one A800-SXM4-80GB per host and CUDA-Q 0.16.0.post1 on both, the FlagQuantum JAX kernel matched CUDA-Q numerically on every configuration measured on both hosts: the largest loss deviation was 1.2e-05 and the largest gradient deviation 1.8e-05 against a 1e-4 tolerance, and every FlagQuantum timing agreed across hosts to within 10 percent. CUDA-Q's nvidia target was faster for forward-only execution at every width, widening from 1.4x at 8 wires to 89x at 22 wires, and that conclusion was insensitive to the warmup count. The FlagQuantum fused value-and-gradient program was faster per call, but its 18-wire ratio moved monotonically from 13.6x to 16.3x between one and five warmups, so an earlier 7.9x reading of the same configuration is withdrawn as under-warmed rather than reproduced.

Landed payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/cudaq_backend_compare_a800_20260930.json`

Reading of that payload: `benchmarks/results/comparison/CUDAQ_BACKEND_COMPARE_A800_20260930.md`

Baseline component ownership:

A domain `cudaq_surface` list is an inventory of the surface a QEC user meets, and an inventory is not an attribution: three components of one product appear in those lists. Most items belong to cudaq-qec, which is the component this domain compares against. The entries below are the items whose owner is a different component, or whose owner is worth stating, and each records what that ownership means for the row it feeds. An attributed item must appear verbatim in exactly one domain surface list, so the table cannot drift from the inventory it explains, and an item owned by another component must state its consequence, so a reader cannot follow the inventory to the wrong owner. Only contested or non-obvious items are listed; the absence of an entry is not a claim about ownership.

| CUDA-Q surface item | Owning component |
| --- | --- |
| detector, detectors, and logical_observable annotations in a kernel | `cudaq-core` |
| dem, dem_from_kernel, and DEMResult | `cudaq-core` |
| extract_syndrome | `cudaq-logical-preview` |
| the logical.* preview namespace | `cudaq-logical-preview` |
| for-stim-users migration | `cudaq-logical-preview` |
| Stim integration | `cudaq-qec` |

- `cudaq-core`, detector, detectors, and logical_observable annotations in a kernel: These annotations are CUDA-Q core kernel syntax rather than a cudaq-qec API, and core's dem_from_kernel is what reads them back. The row the annotations feed therefore belongs to the core capability set, and whether FlagQuantum grows a kernel annotation surface is a language-level decision rather than a QEC library one.
- `cudaq-core`, dem, dem_from_kernel, and DEMResult: One surface item, two owners, so it must be read as two. dem_from_kernel and DEMResult are CUDA-Q core: both are documented on the core Python API page and neither appears in the cudaq-qec Python API, which exposes no dem_from_kernel and no DEMResult anchor at all. cudaq-qec's own construction entries are dem_from_stim_text, dem_from_memory_circuit with its x_ and z_ variants, and dem_from_css_matrices, and cudaq-qec consumes the core record rather than declaring it. Construction is only a cudaq-qec row when it is read against those entries; the core record is a dependency of the row, not its baseline.
- `cudaq-logical-preview`, extract_syndrome: extract_syndrome belongs to the CUDA-Q Logical preview layer, not to cudaq-qec: it appears in that layer's Stim emission material as the encoded operation a fabric call expands into, it is absent from the cudaq-qec Python API, and it is absent from the core Python API page. cudaq-qec's own extraction route is sample_memory_circuit with its x_ and z_ variants, feeding decoder_context_from_memory_circuit. Aligning to the preview layer would not deliver the detector error model this domain is built around, because that layer states of itself that it does not simulate, sample, or decode and emits no detector error models. Either the surface item is misattributed here, or the preview layer is a second target with a different deliverable.
- `cudaq-logical-preview`, the logical.* preview namespace: The namespace is preview-layer scope, not a cudaq-qec surface. The semantic core inside it -- lattice surgery, product rotation, distillation -- is what the qec_logical_operations row tracks through the Qualtran adaptation, while the namespace's patch, gadget, protocol, and program records are that layer's own shape and not a FlagQuantum target.
- `cudaq-logical-preview`, for-stim-users migration: cudaq-qec ships no for-Stim-users page. The only page with that title in the CUDA-Q documentation belongs to the logical preview layer, and it states there that the layer does not simulate, sample, or decode, emits no detector annotations and no detector error models, and that those studies belong to the Stim ecosystem. It is therefore not a cudaq-qec counterpart, and the qec_stim_user_migration document has to be written against cudaq-qec's own surface -- dem_from_stim_text, dem_sampling, the decoder framework, and decoding from Stim DEM text -- rather than translated from that page.
- `cudaq-qec`, Stim integration: Stim appears on both sides of the product split, so the item needs its cudaq-qec half named. Reading Stim detector error model text, and decoding from Stim DEM text, are cudaq-qec's: dem_from_stim_text and the decoder framework's Stim entry point are in the cudaq-qec Python API. Emitting Stim from a verified gadget is the preview layer's and is not a cudaq-qec capability. A row that reads only the second half would compare this repository against a component that does not decode.

- Limitation: A capability absent from this matrix is not evidence that CUDA-Q lacks it; it is evidence that the survey did not record it.
- Limitation: The pinned versions are the ones the repository already targets in contracts/cudaq-export-contract.toml. A CUDA-Q release outside that range requires a new capture.
- Limitation: No row in this file is a performance comparison. Measured numbers belong in benchmarks/results and require an audited payload.
- Limitation: A `runnable` probe is not a recorded measurement. CUDA-Q is not installable from the pinned public index as a binary wheel: the PyPI `cudaq` release is an sdist whose build hook resolves a platform binary distribution at install time. No CI lane in this repository runs either probe, so a payload is only ever captured by hand on a machine that reaches a working CUDA-Q index.
- Limitation: A landed payload describes only the machines, revision, and workload it names. It is not scalability evidence and it does not generalise to other widths, observables, targets, or CUDA-Q releases.
- Limitation: A gradient-path ratio is not a simulation-throughput ratio. The two sides do not execute the same schedule, so a value-and-gradient comparison measures host call structure as well as arithmetic.
- Limitation: The recorded protocol has not been shown to reach steady state for the gradient configurations. A gradient ratio is only meaningful together with the warmup count that produced it, and a settled protocol needs a per-configuration convergence check rather than a fixed warmup count.

No row in this document is a performance comparison or a scalability claim.

### Dependency class of every open gap

The replacement battlefield is the set of capabilities where the CUDA-Q implementation sits on an NVIDIA-proprietary component. Each such capability is a gap FlagQuantum must close with its own kernel or with a FlagOS-family component, not by depending on the NVIDIA original.

### Next work, by priority

**now** (32 open)

- `python_ast_kernel` (language_and_programming_model): The only public way to state a program is the explicit builder API. A restricted Python AST bridge does exist, but it is private Compiler machinery rather than a product surface: flagquantum/compiler/_hybrid/capture.py reads one selected synchronous function through inspect.getsourcelines, it is exported from neither flagquantum nor flagquantum.compiler, and production reaches it only from three flagquantum.qec entry points. So there is no decorator, no kernel type, and no user-facing call form, and the row stays partial rather than supported.
- `kernel_first_class_functions` (language_and_programming_model): The public CircuitIR schema 1.0 has no function or call construct, and the private hybrid program IR does not supply one either: its closed operation vocabulary has no call or function op, capture admits exactly one selected synchronous function, and a hybrid program is a single-function container, so parameters, composition, and nested calls are inexpressible rather than merely unexposed. The planned home this reason previously named, MULTI_LEVEL_IR_ARCHITECTURE.md 5.2, is now labelled a historical design baseline; the level that actually exists is the narrower private profile under flagquantum/compiler/_hybrid, and closing this row needs a call construct, a multi-function container, and a public entry point.
- `classical_control_flow` (language_and_programming_model): Implemented, but only inside the private hybrid compiler and without a while form. flagquantum/compiler/_hybrid carries classical values with real def-use (Value and ValueId, Operation, Block, Region) and an SSA verifier; if branches both compile-time-resolved and measurement-driven; and for loops over range, enumerate, and statically ranked tensors with explicit region-carried results and a bounded unroll ceiling. Straight-line local temporaries and outer-name rebinding are supported. Three flagquantum.qec entry points consume it in production. What is missing is the cudaq baseline in the row title: while, break, continue, and for-else are refused with an exact diagnostic, and there is no public kernel surface, so a user reaches none of this directly. That is why the row is partial and not supported.
- `control_adjoint_modifiers` (language_and_programming_model): The adjoint half is present on the Stable Core type: Circuit.adjoint() inverts a program by reversing its instruction order and inverting each instruction from the rule its opcode declares, inverting an instruction that carries a matrix by conjugate transpose, and refusing a noise channel, a dynamic operation, a classically conditioned instruction, a matrix without a conjugate transpose and an unknown opcode without a matrix with CapabilityError instead of copying them forward. 31 of the 35 registered opcodes invert. The control half is absent: only the named gates ccx and cswap provide multi-controlled forms, no controlled-modifier constructor exists, and a unitary passed through Circuit.any is not a modifier. `power` is absent for the same reason. Neither gap has an approved API change proposal, so both are owned rather than partially built.
- `type_system_qubit_register_view` (language_and_programming_model): CircuitIR 1.0 addresses wires by integer index and has no type system, and the private hybrid program IR does not close that: its IRType vocabulary is bool, index, quantum.effect, and scalar and tensor forms, and a qubit stays an index value. What the private level does have is a real linearity rule, enforced by its verifier rather than asserted -- the quantum effect is the linear type, and reusing it or dropping it fails closed -- but the linear subject is the effect token, not a qubit, and nothing models a register or a view over one. A qubit, qvector, and qview type with linearity over the qubits themselves is absent.
- `dynamic_kernel_measurement_feedback` (language_and_programming_model): FlagQuantum implements this through runtime/dynamic with a candidate-stable public namespace. The registered level is below production, and the surface is narrower than the CUDA-Q baseline.
- `custom_operation_registration` (language_and_programming_model): Circuit.any accepts a raw unitary but there is no operation registry, no schema, and no backend degradation contract for a user-defined operation.
- `pass_manager_and_pass_plugins` (compiler_and_ir): The pass and analysis contracts and the CompilerPassExtension protocol are designed, and the ecosystem SDK exposes the extension kind, but no pass manager consumes the protocol and compilation paths remain fixed pipelines.
- `topology_aware_routing` (compiler_and_ir): Routing, topology legalization, and directional topology modules exist as a skeleton, but there is no published-quality router comparable to a SABRE-class algorithm.
- `qir_code_generation` (compiler_and_ir): The earlier reason on this row was wrong and is replaced by measurement: FlagQuantum does not emit OpenQASM and QCIS text only. `flagquantum/compiler/qir.py` emits QIR base-profile LLVM IR -- a `FlagQuantumEntryPoint` definition carrying the `entry_point` attribute, `__quantum__qis__*` calls for the lowered program, `__quantum__qis__mz__body` for each measured wire, `__quantum__rt__tuple_record_output` and `__quantum__rt__result_record_output` for the output, the declarations those calls need, and the `qir_major_version`/`qir_minor_version`/`dynamic_qubit_management`/`dynamic_result_management` module flags -- and it is reachable from the public compiler surface, since `translate(program, format="qir-2.0")` is one of the four `TRANSLATION_FORMATS` and `target_emission` carries a `qir-2.0` profile whose emitter is this function. QIR is vendor-neutral, so the whole path is software this programme can own. The reason the row is `partial` rather than `supported` is the half of CUDA-Q's row that is absent: CUDA-Q generates *Profile-QIR*, and this emitter is the base profile only. The adaptive profile is absent, and with both dynamic-management module flags `false` so are `__quantum__rt__qubit_allocate_array`, `__quantum__rt__qubit_release_array`, and every `read_result` call, which is the same gap the runtime qubit allocation row records from the IR side. Pulse-level generation and runtime library extension calls are absent, only the constant-index pointer kind is emitted, and there is no LLVM compilation to an object file or an executable: this is text, and no external QIR validator was run against it, so conformance is the repository's own semantic check plus a host C parser accepting the text as LLVM IR syntax. An opcode with no QIS instruction is lowered to a native sequence equal to the requested gate up to an unconditional global phase the base profile cannot express, and a gate the profile cannot carry is refused by index and opcode rather than approximated.
- `compiler_plugin_ecosystem` (compiler_and_ir): The extension protocol and lifecycle exist, but no discovery path reaches compilation, so an out-of-tree pass cannot run.
- `backend_multi_gpu_statevector` (simulation_backends): Sharded statevector training exists at development_evidence level with one measured 32-qubit complex128 forward pass on one eight-accelerator node. Production capacity expansion is not established.
- `backend_tensor_network_exact` (simulation_backends): A self-built PyTorch tensor-network path exists without a cuTensorNet-class contraction planner, so the exact regime is narrower than the CUDA-Q baseline.
- `backend_density_matrix` (simulation_backends): An engine exists in the simulation domain, but it has no capability-maturity.toml entry, so it carries no recorded owner, limitation set, or hardware evidence.
- `backend_stim_stabilizer` (simulation_backends): Both halves of the row now exist in a narrower form. The representation half is closed: a Stim-backed Clifford sampling engine samples a thousand-wire GHZ chain, so the wire counts a dense amplitude store cannot hold are reachable, and Stim is Apache-2.0 licensed and independent of every NVIDIA component, which is why this was integration rather than research. The execution half landed as an execution mode: `plan` and `run` reach the engine through `state_mode='stabilizer'` and report a plan, a result, and execution evidence, which `tests/integration/test_stabilizer_execution_mode.py` pins. What remains is narrower than the baseline in three ways: no expectation values over the representation, no noise, and no detector error model connected to it.
- `backend_dynamics` (simulation_backends): FlagQuantum has a real Lindblad engine with RK4 integration, validation codes, and evidence fields, so this capability is not missing. Three walls separate it from the baseline: CPU-only hard rejection, a dense four-to-the-n Hamiltonian with a fixed step, and a static Hamiltonian. Batching and gradients are rejected.
- `kraus_channel_algebra` (noise_and_error_models): A general Kraus constructor exists and is validated. `KrausChannel` accepts an arbitrary operator list, refuses a set that is not trace-preserving (completeness compared at `atol = rtol = 1e-6`) and a dimension that is not a positive power of two, serializes through the `flagquantum.kraus_channel.v1` schema, and reaches simulation through `NoiseModel.add` and `Circuit.noisy_density_matrix`. What is absent is the operator type the CUDA-Q surface builds a channel from: no matrix-valued operator participates in operator algebra, which is the gap `matrix_and_custom_operator` already records.
- `detector_error_model` (noise_and_error_models): Both directions of the stim text interchange work. `from_memory_circuit` builds a model exactly for Pauli noise over the reference Clifford gate set; `to_stim_text` emits text stim 1.16.0 parses; `from_stim_text` reads everything stim wrote in a 240-model developer-time sweep except a `repeat` block, and `str(model.flattened())` is a complete route around that one refusal; both readings of a `^` separator are offered under upstream's own `use_decomp_suggestions` flag name, and the default is the one stim itself means, measured against stim's own sampler rather than asserted. The model can also state that mechanisms are alternatives rather than independent, which is the one thing its parity matrices cannot carry: an error id groups them, the marginal rates and the sampler read a group as one fault, and the text writer refuses an id-carrying model instead of printing an independent one under the same probabilities. The row stays partial because conversion is narrower than the baseline at the input end: `from_memory_circuit` accepts one circuit record and one noise record, so an arbitrary circuit carrying detector and observable annotations has no route to a model, and a non-Pauli channel is refused rather than decomposed. `flagquantum/qec/IMPLEMENTATION.md` records the sweeps and the arithmetic.
- `spin_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): Pauli observables exist. Operator arithmetics for products, sums, scalars, exponentials, commutators, and anticommutators are absent.
- `super_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): The algebra is implemented: `flagquantum/operators/superoperator.py` states a superoperator as a sum of `coefficient * left @ state @ right` terms, where a missing side is a one-sided multiplication, with the three CUDA-Q constructors and an accumulating `+=`; `apply` and `dense` are two independent formulas in the repository-wide row-major vectorization `vec(A rho B) = (A (x) B^T) vec(rho)`, and the Lindblad generator assembled that way is the same arithmetic as `Liouvillian.dense()`, so the check that used to read 4.441e-16 now reads exactly 0.0. What is absent is everything beyond construction and the two views: no Choi, PTM, or Kraus representation transform, no partial trace, and no adjoint on the algebra. The factor contract has two implementations, `torch.Tensor` and `PauliSum`, both supplying `__matmul__`, `__rmatmul__` and `dense()`, so a matrix-free Hamiltonian enters a term without being materialized. The row stays partial rather than supported because CUDA-Q's row is about superoperator representations and this is the construction-and-evaluation half.
- `chemistry_domain_library` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): The ansatz half exists and the integrals half does not. `flagquantum/algorithms/chemistry.py` enumerates the single and double excitations of an electron count in a spin-orbital count, builds the fermionic generator of one, emits the exact circuit that realizes its exponential, composes them into the UCCSD circuit, and covers a hardware-efficient and a coupler hardware-efficient ansatz with a parameter count; the gate sequences are the ones CUDA-Q's own kernels apply, so a workload built around them transfers. What is absent is the first entry point this row names: there is no PySCF or other driver dependency, so no molecular Hamiltonian, no basis set, no active space, no Hartree-Fock solve, and no energy reference arrives from here. Two divergences from the baseline are deliberate and stated rather than silent: an occupied index above a virtual one is refused instead of emitting an empty ladder that would be a local rotation rather than an excitation, and `uccsd_excitations` fills the lowest n_electrons spin orbitals where CUDA-Q's `get_uccsd_excitations` divides by two before rounding up, so the two agree on even electron counts only.
- `execution_entry_points` (algorithm_layer): Run, counts, expectation, compile, and plan exist. evolve and translate have no equivalent, and draw exists in a narrower form.
- `error_mitigation` (algorithm_layer): Zero-noise extrapolation and probabilistic error cancellation, not Clifford data regression. An observable is measured at several error strengths by scaling the one error-probability parameter each noise channel declares, and the curve is continued to zero by polynomial least squares or Richardson extrapolation, which reports the residual it left and the variance amplification of its weights. The channel families whose parameters are not error probabilities are refused by name, and a model that declares a readout rule is refused rather than measured without it, because the estimate is Tr(O rho) and classical readout confusion is applied after measurement. Beside that, a channel the model declares as a Pauli channel is inverted exactly by decomposing its inverse into a signed combination of Pauli words read off its Pauli transfer matrix, one location at a time, which reports the sampling overhead gamma squared that a sampled implementation would pay and refuses by measured magnitude the channel families whose transfer matrix is not diagonal and the channels whose transfer eigenvalue reaches zero. Readout-error mitigation and Clifford data regression are absent.
- `variational_algorithms` (algorithm_layer): VQE-class and several algorithm primitives exist as separate registered capabilities rather than a solver family, so the surface shape differs from the baseline.
- `qec_code_library` (quantum_error_correction): The repetition code, the rotated surface code and the Steane code are declared as code records and each produces a memory-experiment source with detector and observable layouts, so a distance-d rotated patch is expressible and a code carrying both a Z-type and an X-type readout is expressible through Steane. A code record can now also be read into matrices rather than only into a circuit: css_code_matrices lifts its four blocks into a CssCodeMatrices record, which carries hz, hx, lz and lx together, so a code whose stabilizers are known reaches a code-capacity detector error model on either readout basis without a gadget being built for it and without losing a fault family. The families remain declared rather than constructed, and an arbitrary parity-check matrix still has no route in: a check states one ancilla and one CNOT direction fixed by its type, so a mixed X-and-Z stabilizer is refused, and a logical observable that is neither pure X nor pure Z is refused rather than half-read, so qLDPC, Reichardt and Floquet codes are absent and a colour code has no record even though the CSS shape now admits one. The code records themselves still expose no decode entry point, because decoding belongs to the decoder row and reads a detector error model rather than a code. The noise record states a rate per fault family and the same rate per element, so a per-location profile is expressible: the four scalars and their per-qubit and per-check overrides are PhenomenologicalNoise's, read against the code's own vectors.
- `qec_decoder_family` (quantum_error_correction): Matching is now self-implemented rather than absent: the detector error model becomes a weighted decoding graph whose edge weight is log((1 - p) / p), and a syndrome is decoded exactly by enumerating the ways to pair its defective detectors and to route any of them to the graph's boundary. The row stays partial on scope, not on correctness. Matching needs a graphlike model and refuses a hyperedge rather than projecting it onto a pair, so a code whose mechanisms flip three or more detectors is outside this row's matching half. The pairing is enumerated, so a syndrome is bounded by a defect budget instead of decoded at scale. Belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding is absent, so the LDPC codes the baseline serves with it are not served here; the sliding-window decoder for a long-lived experiment is absent; and there is no decoder registry or plugin protocol, so a decoder is constructed directly rather than requested by name. The baseline's GPU decoders are deliberately not chased, because the CUDA-Q qLDPC decoder is a closed-source shared library, so only its interface position is a target and an Apache-2.0 implementation is the route if that scope is ever reached. The row fails closed on a second gap of its own: because the graph keeps one edge per mechanism, a model that states one detector-and-observable signature twice would become two parallel edges and the matcher would take the cheaper, so the decoder requires a unique signature before it weights anything and refuses a duplicate with the merge that resolves it named in the refusal. It fails closed on the neighbouring statement for the neighbouring reason: a model that says two mechanisms are alternatives is refused and the groups are named, because one weight per mechanism is the weight of a fault that fires alone while a group of alternatives is one fault whose weight is the negative log-likelihood of the group, so weighting the members separately would charge the model more than the fault costs. The cross-check half has landed and it is a comparison of two selections rather than an equality of two instruments: PyMatching is behind the `pymatching` extra and is never the authority, and because its own accumulator reports 3.9020747171643912 for a mechanism this row states as 3.9020746947749574 the graph it minimizes over is not exactly this one. The row therefore asserts the cheapest weight on every syndrome, the observables wherever the cheapest explanation is unique, and the two refusals as the same set, with a pinned tie on the distance-three repetition code so the tie clause is demonstrated. The registry, the two decoder families the matcher does not cover, and the hyperedge front end were the work this row still named; of those, the registry has landed and is described above. A decoder registry has since landed, and it is the factory half of the baseline's decoder surface rather than the whole of it: flagquantum.qec.get_decoder(name, source, **options) reaches a decoder by name and flagquantum.qec.register_decoder(name, *, replace=False) puts one there, with registration checked while the registering module is imported so a class missing decode or from_detector_error_model is refused there rather than at the first caller. The registry is deliberately narrower than upstream's. Its source argument takes the three carriers a caller can hold a model in -- the detector error model, stim's text for one, and the decoding graph the model defines -- and not H_or_dem_text_or_sparse_matrix, because lifting a parity-check matrix would also mean choosing the noise model and round count that from_code_matrices reads rather than defaults. It holds the detector-error-model family alone, because the repetition-code decoders here take an ordered syndrome history rather than detection events and one name space over two input protocols would make a name mean one of two things. It fails closed rather than falling back: an unregistered name raises and lists the registered names, a source that is not one of the three carriers is refused by type, and no name is preferred over another, so the authority is returned for its own name wherever the optional extra happens to be installed. The remaining work inside this row is therefore the two decoder families the matcher does not cover, the hyperedge front end, and the plugin boundary the baseline ships -- the registered adapter is a concrete class under a name rather than a plugin loaded across a version boundary.
- `qec_stim_integration` (quantum_error_correction): All three halves now exist, and the row is partial on scope rather than on connection. Stim-backed sampling landed with the stabilizer engine, the detector error model half landed with the text reader and its own capability entry, and the join landed last: a memory circuit is lowered once, each configured noise location is placed at the instruction it belongs to, the result is executed on the stabilizer engine, and the detection events and observable flips are read off the recorded bits. A decoder built from that same circuit's model then decodes those events, so a logical-failure rate no longer needs the statevector ceiling that bounds construction. What the row still lacks is breadth of the noise grammar: a location is a data flip at a round boundary or a measurement flip at a check's readout, which is what the phenomenological record names, while a channel placed after an arbitrary gate has no location and is still declined. The x_ and z_ variants are absent for the same reason the code record is a Z-memory record. Decoding itself stays with the decoder row rather than being implied here. The row names three registry entries because the implementation genuinely spans three: the sampling half is `stabilizer_sampling`, the interchange half is `detector_error_model`, and the join that consumes both is `qec_memory_circuit_sampling`. The row is read only against cudaq-qec, which is where the detector error models live; where the two components divide this surface is recorded in `baseline.surface_ownership`.
- `third_party_target_sdk` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Partial. A third party declares its target in an extension manifest and FlagQuantum validates the declaration fail-closed and turns it into a capability snapshot (`flagquantum/ecosystem/extensions/target_sdk.py`, restored with 8 tests). What is absent is execution through that target: a registered description is not yet a runnable backend, so a provider still cannot be added end to end without changing FlagQuantum.
- `provider_roster_breadth` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Partial. IonQ, Quantinuum, IQM, and neutral-atom declarations are read fail-closed into backend profiles, preflighted locally, and driven through the existing `remote/qpu` provider contract, alongside the existing Quafu, Braket, and Azure adapters. Still absent: photonic and quantum-control-system providers, an analog-schedule submission path for neutral atoms, and any hardware evidence, because no adapter has been exercised against a live provider.
- `simulator_plugin_admission` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): The decisive ecosystem gap. The extension protocol exists with an entry-point group, manifest, SDK version check, capability negotiation, and an ExecutionBackendExtension contract, and the runtime has a separate backend capability registry. The two never import each other, so an extension can be negotiated and discovered but cannot execute.
- `large_scale_statevector` (performance_and_scalability): The measured FlagQuantum point is a 32-qubit complex128 forward pass on one eight-accelerator node, which is a development-evidence result and is not comparable to the baseline scale. No row here is a performance claim.
- `production_sharded_statevector` (performance_and_scalability): The registered level is below production, so the sharded path cannot support a capacity-expansion claim yet.

**next** (33 open)

- `runtime_qubit_allocation` (language_and_programming_model): Wire count is fixed at circuit construction. Runtime allocation is designed in the QuantumIR level and is not implemented.
- `pauli_tracking_sbe` (language_and_programming_model): The sampling engine and the detector error model module both exist, so the condition this row was deferred on is met, and the row is now blocked on one narrower thing: the engine refuses a circuit carrying any noise instruction rather than tracking a Pauli frame through it. Pauli tracking is what would let a noisy Clifford circuit be sampled without a dense state.
- `global_seed_control` (language_and_programming_model): Seeding is per call rather than process wide. `ExecutionOptions` carries a seed and the training path carries its own seeder, so a user reproduces a run by threading a seed through each entry point instead of stating one seed for the session.
- `gate_decomposition_patterns` (compiler_and_ir): Native gate legalization exists but there is no rule library, so a target basis outside the legalization table cannot be reached.
- `basis_conversion` (compiler_and_ir): Partial coverage follows from the legalization table; there is no general conversion between two arbitrary named bases.
- `clifford_t_synthesis` (compiler_and_ir): Absent. The algorithms are published and vendor-neutral, and any implementation needs exact arithmetic that FlagQuantum does not currently carry.
- `angle_synthesis` (compiler_and_ir): Absent, and it shares the exact-arithmetic requirement with Clifford+T synthesis.
- `commutation_aware_rewrite` (compiler_and_ir): The analysis and one rewrite consumer are implemented. `flagquantum/compiler/commutation.py` answers the two questions a reduction needs -- whether two instructions commute, and which instructions form one commuting block on a wire -- and its rule source is a source of proof rather than of record: it reads the two instructions' operator schemas and proves the commutation, with disjoint support unconditional and a gate the rule source has no rule for treated as a barrier. `flagquantum/compiler/commutation_cancellation.py` is the consumer: `cancel_commuting_self_inverse` removes parameter-free, matrix-free members of the self-inverse set in proven pairs, keeping the last member of an odd group so what the block preserves is applied as late as it was before, and it is scheduled inside the pipeline's fixed-point loop, so `cx(0, 1) rz(0) cx(0, 1)` reduces to `rz(0)` where the wire-local self-inverse merge could not see it. What is absent is the part CUDA-Q's row is named for. CUDA-Q's pass is a driver: `CommutationAwareRewriteMatcher` searches backward from an anchor operation for the nearest earlier endpoint that a consumer will accept, crossing a frontier only where pairwise commutation or disjoint support is proven, and the consumer owns the endpoint's algebraic identity. FlagQuantum has one consumer hard-coded against the analysis instead of a matcher a second rewrite can plug into, so no pass can reorder a gate past a commuter to expose a cancellation that a different pass then takes. There is also no per-block analysis invalidation, because there is no pass manager to invalidate through, and no linear-use-def guard, because `CircuitIR` is a straight-line instruction list in which nothing can branch: the same fact that makes the guard unnecessary here is what makes the search unnecessary, which is why the two are one gap rather than two.
- `dead_code_elimination` (compiler_and_ir): Absent, and the earlier reason this row gave -- that it depends on the pass infrastructure -- does not survive measurement, because the neighbouring commutation row was reconciled without any pass infrastructure at all. CUDA-Q's pass does two things, and neither has a representation here. It removes a `quake.null_wire` whose only use is `quake.sink`, and a `quake.alloca` whose only use is its matching `quake.dealloc` or which has no use at all. `CircuitIR` declares its width once as `n_wires` and the operator schema table holds no allocation, release, null-wire, or sink opcode, so a wire that was never allocated cannot exist and the object this elimination removes is not denotable. What is left is the general half -- a gate whose result no later reader observes -- and that is where the semantics first have to be settled, because the answer differs by output class. `fq.run` returns the whole statevector, so a gate on a wire nothing else touches is observable in the returned state and eliminating it would change the result; a program that declares `measurements` or `observables` has named its outputs, and only there can a wire with no reader be dead. A pass written against one reading would be wrong for the other, and no such declaration of output class is a property of `CircuitIR` today: an empty measurements tuple means both `the caller wants no measurement` and `the state is the answer`. That distinction is the work this row is actually waiting on, and it is recorded rather than implied.
- `target_text_emitters` (compiler_and_ir): An OpenQASM emitter exists. The emitter set is narrower than the CUDA-Q roster.
- `resource_estimation` (compiler_and_ir): The static half exists. `flagquantum/compiler/resource_estimation.py` reports the operation count per opcode, the schedule depth, the per-wire depth, the widest operation, the T family and its depth, the channel count, and the declared register width, over the instruction sequence the caller wrote, with the basis named in the record as `static_instruction_sequence`. It refuses a program whose sequence has data dependence, naming the instruction index, and that refusal is what the row now turns on: a straight-line list has no loop bound, so loops and functions stay unestimatable until ProgramIR exists, exactly as this row recorded before any of the rest was built. The estimate is also not a latency and not a device cost -- no gate duration, connectivity, or routing overhead enters it -- and no basis conversion runs, so the counts are of the opcodes the caller wrote rather than of a lowered basis. Qubit peak is not a separate field; the register width and the used wires are. The fault-tolerant layer above the tally landed separately, as `flagquantum.algorithms.logical_resources` charging the tally on a rotated surface code.
- `foreign_circuit_import` (compiler_and_ir): The Qiskit direction exists: an ecosystem adapter builds a FlagQuantum circuit from a provider object. OpenQASM import does not, and the OpenQASM surface FlagQuantum carries is an emitter, so a circuit that exists only as text cannot enter the framework.
- `backend_asynchronous_multi_qpu` (simulation_backends): Absent. FlagQuantum has single-target remote execution but no asynchronous fan-out across several QPUs with independent result streams.
- `backend_gpu_fabric` (simulation_backends): Absent as a FlagQuantum-owned transport. The replacement target is a FlagOS-family collective layer, not NCCL.
- `dynamics_schedule_and_integrators` (simulation_backends): The Lindblad engine integrates with one fixed-step RK4 over an explicitly declared time grid and a static Hamiltonian. There is no schedule object carrying time-dependent coefficients and no selectable integrator, so accuracy and stiffness cannot be traded per problem.
- `noise_model_callback` (noise_and_error_models): Per-gate (`NoiseModel.add(gate_names, channel)`) and per-qubit (`wires=`) static injection both exist, and lowering now refuses a rule that cannot apply. The callback form is absent, and `NoiseRule` carries a `KrausChannel` fixed at construction. A callback cannot be added to `NoiseRule` as it stands: `NoiseModel.identity` is a SHA-256 digest of `to_dict()`, and checkpoint resume and execution-plan identity both bind to it, so a channel chosen by an arbitrary callable would make identity unreproducible. Any such rule must be registered under a declared name and parameterization before it can participate in a model identity.
- `batched_trajectory` (noise_and_error_models): Trajectory simulation exists; batched execution across trajectories is narrower than the baseline.
- `unitary_mixture_degradation` (noise_and_error_models): The distinction is made in the noise layer and is decided by the operators rather than by the channel's name: `KrausChannel.unitary_mixture` reports the branches and their weights, and the criterion is that every operator is a non-negative real scale times a unitary, with the whole Gram matrix checked rather than its leading entry, so an amplitude damping channel is refused for its unequal singular values. A zero-weight operator is a branch of probability zero and is dropped rather than read as a general channel, so every built-in factory stays classified at the edges of its range. One consumer reads the answer: the stabilizer positioned-noise entry point executes a one- or two-wire channel whose branches are Pauli frames and refuses every other channel by name, so a depolarizing channel samples as its four frames where it previously refused. Two limits keep the row partial. The framework comparison gives no Python accessor for the property at all, so there is no external surface to conform against and the contract here is FlagQuantum's own. And only one consumer reads it: the density-matrix and trajectory routes execute a general channel without asking whether it is a mixture, so the sampling advantage a mixture allows is unrealised there.
- `noise_trajectory_shot_allocation` (noise_and_error_models): FlagQuantum samples Kraus trajectories, but the trajectory choice belongs to the engine rather than to the caller: the MPS trajectory path draws them implicitly and exposes an ensemble size, so there is no trajectory enumeration, no ordered or probabilistic selection strategy, and no shot-allocation policy. Those strategies are the whole of this row.
- `fermion_operator_algebra` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): The algebra and one mapping exist. `flagquantum/observables/fermion.py` builds a normal-ordered sum over spin orbitals with `create`, `annihilate`, and `number`; addition, subtraction, unary negation, scalar multiplication, `*`, `dagger`, `commutator`, and `anticommutator` are all present, so a chemistry workload's generator is an expression rather than a hand-applied relation, and equality is structural, which makes `is_hermitian` exact rather than a tolerance test. `jordan_wigner` maps a Hermitian operator to the Pauli `Observable` the existing statevector path already measures, which is how a fermionic observable acquires a value. What is absent is the rest of the mapping family this row's own wording names: Bravyi-Kitaev, parity, and ternary-tree encodings do not exist, and neither does any reduction in the Pauli weight of the image, which is the reason those encodings exist at all. The mode count is an argument rather than inferred, and no matrix form of a fermionic operator ships.
- `matrix_and_custom_operator` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): A stable operator schema and discovery interface exist, and a matrix can now enter the superoperator algebra as a term factor. What is still missing is a matrix-valued operator type in the operator algebra itself: no `MatrixOperator` or `custom_op` type composes with `Observable` or the fermionic sum through products, sums, scalars, adjoints, or commutators, and the superoperator factor contract is deliberately narrower than that, requiring only `__matmul__`, `__rmatmul__` and `dense()`.
- `exponential_pauli_operator` (operator_algebra_and_domain_libraries): The dense constructor exists: `flagquantum/simulation/pauli.py` reads a Pauli word and its targets positionally, so character `i` of the word acts on `targets[i]`, and returns the operator the pair denotes on a declared number of wires. A Pauli product squares to the identity, so the exponential is evaluated in closed form as `exp(-i theta P) = cos(theta) I - i sin(theta) P` rather than by exponentiating a matrix; the form is exact at every angle and is checked against an eigendecomposition of the product and against the defining series of the exponential. An `I` character consumes its target and contributes no support, so a word aligns with a wire list without dropping the wires it does not act on, and an all-identity word returns the global phase it denotes instead of the identity. A word whose length disagrees with the number of targets, a character outside `X`, `Y`, `Z` and `I`, a repeated target, a target outside the declared wires, and a non-finite angle are each refused. What is absent is the circuit-level form, and it is the whole of the row: no operation the IR carries and no compiler pattern decomposes it into single-qubit basis changes and a CNOT chain, so a circuit cannot contain an exponential of a Pauli product, no rotation parameter reaches it as a differentiable value, and `pauli_word` is not a value type a kernel parameter can be written with. The dense constructor is the operator those three would be built from.
- `state_and_unitary_access` (algorithm_layer): Circuit.state exists. A full unitary accessor is absent.
- `algorithm_block_encoding_family` (algorithm_layer): Two members of the family are implemented natively and the rest are absent. Trotter time evolution landed as flagquantum.algorithms.trotter: a weighted Pauli sum becomes an ordinary Circuit through a product formula of order 1 or 2, with the exact circuit for one Pauli word's exponential as its primitive. Block encoding landed next as flagquantum.algorithms.primitives.block_encoding, promoted out of the private helper flagquantum.algorithms.svd held, and it carries the qubitization walk step with it: the reflection is emitted as one dense matrix, the flagged block is the matrix over the caller's subnormalisation, and one walk step is a rotation whose eigenphases are the arccosines of the encoded eigenvalues. The fermion-qubit transform family already had jordan_wigner at flagquantum.observables.fermion. Still absent: qubitization as a public walk object carrying a moment count, the Pauli linear-combination encoding, QSVT, double factorization, and the Bravyi-Kitaev, parity and ternary-tree transforms. The row names two registry entries because the two shipped members are separate capabilities with separate surfaces and separate evidence: the product formula and the block encoding share the family and nothing else. The plan's original route -- adapt Qualtran, Apache-2.0, which covers the same mathematics -- was ruled out by the repository owner: Qualtran 0.7.0 carries 27 transitive dependencies and is not declared in dependency-policy.toml, so the mathematics is implemented natively instead and no third-party quantum-algorithm library is a dependency.
- `optimizer_library` (algorithm_layer): The gradient-based half is wider than the baseline's: the training path takes a PyTorch optimizer and the staged hybrid optimizer accepts adam, adamw, sgd, and LBFGS. The gradient-free half is now partly closed. SPSA is implemented as a standalone optimizer that consumes a plain objective callable and a parameter tensor instead of a gradient, and it spends two objective evaluations per step whatever the parameter count, which is the same recursion cudaq.optimizers exposes; the parity entry records its boundary rather than a convergence claim, and the estimator is biased rather than a gradient. COBYLA and NelderMead are still absent, and the training entry point still refuses an optimizer that is not a PyTorch one, so an SPSA run is a caller-owned loop and not an fq.train call.
- `classical_data_encoding` (algorithm_layer): Both entry points exist in the Algorithms layer and cover the classical front end, but the CUDA-Q contract is not reached. amplitude_encode here returns a Circuit whose preparation is delegated to the existing arbitrary_state primitive after padding to the next power of two with a caller-chosen value and normalising by the euclidean norm; CUDA-Q's amplitude_encode instead returns a data-carrying State and is re-normalised after padding rather than before, and there is no route that takes an existing State. angular_encode and append_angular_encode match CUDA-Q's axis semantics exactly, one rx/ry/rz per wire with 'X'/'Y'/'Z' case-insensitive and 'Y' the default, and the append form is what a data-reuploading map composes from. What is absent is the kernel-language form, which CUDA-Q intercepts in the compiler and which has no analogue here because no kernel front end exists, and the block-encoding-style padding contract over an amplitude input.
- `qec_stim_user_migration` (quantum_error_correction): Absent, and its upstream counterpart is not where the surface list implies. cudaq-qec publishes no for-Stim-users page: the only page with that title in the CUDA-Q documentation belongs to the logical preview layer, and it states there that the layer does not simulate, sample, or decode, emits no detector annotations and no detector error models, and that those studies belong to the Stim ecosystem. So the document cannot be translated from that page, and reading the row's name as pointing at it would aim a `next`-priority capability at a component that produces no detector error model. The counterpart is cudaq-qec's own Stim surface: reading Stim detector error model text through dem_from_stim_text, sampling a model through dem_sampling, and decoding from a Stim DEM through the decoder framework. The document is conformance work rather than a new implementation, so it is still sequenced after the Stim integration row's halves are joined; until then a migration guide would describe a route that stops at the join.
- `logical_resource_estimation` (logical_and_ftqc_layer): A rotated-surface-code cost over the compiler's own static estimate rather than a second tally: flagquantum.algorithms.logical_resources reads the operation counts, the T family, and the schedule depth from flagquantum.compiler.resource_estimation.estimate_resources and adds the code layer, at a distance the caller names, as 2 d^2 - 1 physical qubits per patch and d surface-code cycles per logical layer. The row is partial for three named reasons. The input has to already be Clifford+T: a parametric rotation is refused rather than synthesised, because angle synthesis is absent and a T-count taken over an un-synthesised angle would be the count of a circuit nobody will run, and a compound operation whose T-count is its decomposition's -- a Toffoli, a controlled swap -- is refused, because a Toffoli is not a Clifford gate and the decompositions do not agree on what it costs. There is no distillation factory, magic-state budget, routing overhead, placement, scheduling, or device model, so the physical figure is a floor for a circuit of these layers rather than a compiled estimate. And no logical error rate is reported, because a threshold fit's prefactor and threshold are a device's numbers rather than this unit's. Clifford+T synthesis, angle synthesis, and the arithmetic constructions are the moves that would take this row to supported.
- `runtime_endpoint` (hardware_and_cloud_targets): Absent as a named contract. FlagQuantum has remote adapters and a deployment surface, but no provider-neutral endpoint object.
- `realtime_feedback_loop` (realtime_control): Blocked, not merely absent. The software half of the surface now exists in flagquantum/remote/realtime, but the microsecond feedback loop itself needs an FPGA and a remote-direct-memory-access capable network interface, so it cannot be closed by software at all and is delivered, if at all, with a hardware partner. ARCH-013 records it as an owned blocked row rather than as a plan.
- `realtime_transport` (realtime_control): Partly closed and still not a transport. The vendor-neutral messaging protocol and the device-call channel seam a transport plugs into now exist in flagquantum/remote/realtime, with the slot framing, payload type system, status convention, and function table specified and exercised offline. What remains absent is the transport itself: RoCE and Ethernet carriage, a ring buffer, a dispatcher, and every timing property, none of which software alone can supply. The row stays unsupported so the dependency-class accounting is not flattered by a protocol that measures nothing.
- `realtime_host_api` (realtime_control): Partly delivered. The vendor-neutral half is the messaging protocol and the device-call abstraction, and both are now implemented and conformance-checked offline in flagquantum/remote/realtime: a fixed-size slot, a typed payload declared by a handler schema, a function table keyed by a hashed handler name, a status convention, and a channel resolved by name at runtime. What keeps the row at partial rather than supported is the other half of the host-facing surface: the dispatcher, the ring buffer, the function-table launch path, and the occupancy and graph entry points are absent by design, because they belong to the hardware partner and to a device runtime this repository does not own.
- `distribution_packaging` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): FlagQuantum ships a single package plus a development container. A metapackage that selects a FlagOS and accelerator generation has no equivalent and is needed for a domestic-accelerator install story.

The row stays partial because the algebra still has no consumer and no execution path: there is no bosonic or photonic backend, no Fock-space state, no expectation value, and no qubit mapping for a bosonic operator, so the dense form is a reference and a test oracle rather than a production route. The truncation dimension is the caller's because the commutation relations live on untruncated monomials -- the commutator of two truncated ladder matrices differs from the identity at the top level -- and only the explicit dimension says which operator a caller's numbers describe.

Of those three, product rotation is present: `certify_logical_product` checks a candidate single-patch Pauli product against the code's own checks and its same-type stabilizer span, and `derive_anticommuting_logical_product` solves the code's opposite-type checks over GF(2) for the partner of a declared observable, so one code record is read out in either Pauli basis and the detector error model of a rotated frame carries observable-live mechanisms that the default frame does not. - `vendor_certification` (engineering_ecosystem_and_abi): Absent. FlagQuantum evidence governance is stronger than the baseline in maturity levels and benchmark auditing, but there is no certification path by which a vendor attests to a backend.

### Capability detail

#### Language and programming model

Domain id: `language_and_programming_model`

CUDA-Q surface: nvq++, @cudaq.kernel, kernel arguments, classical control flow, cudaq.control, cudaq.adjoint, register_operation, qudit and photonic operations

| Capability | CUDA-Q baseline | Status | Priority | Dependency class | FlagQuantum maturity | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cpp_kernel_frontend` | C++ front end nvq++ compiling Clang AST into the Quake dialect | unsupported | later | B_open_neutral | none | No C++ product surface exists. A domestic C++ front end would reuse the same LLVM/MLIR upstream as the Python path, so it is deferred rather than excluded. |
| `python_ast_kernel` | @cudaq.kernel decorator compiling a Python function body through an AST bridge | partial | now | none | none | The only public way to state a program is the explicit builder API. A restricted Python AST bridge does exist, but it is private Compiler machinery rather than a product surface: flagquantum/compiler/_hybrid/capture.py reads one selected synchronous function through inspect.getsourcelines, it is exported from neither flagquantum nor flagquantum.compiler, and production reaches it only from three flagquantum.qec entry points. So there is no decorator, no kernel type, and no user-facing call form, and the row stays partial rather than supported. |

The planned home this reason previously named, MULTI_LEVEL_IR_ARCHITECTURE.md 5.2, is now labelled a historical design baseline; the level that actually exists is the narrower private profile under flagquantum/compiler/_hybrid, and closing this row needs a call construct, a multi-function container, and a public entry point. |

Straight-line local temporaries and outer-name rebinding are supported. Three flagquantum.qec entry points consume it in production. What is missing is the cudaq baseline in the row title: while, break, continue, and for-else are refused with an exact diagnostic, and there is no public kernel surface, so a user reaches none of this directly. That is why the row is partial and not supported. |

#### Compiler and intermediate representation

Domain id: `compiler_and_ir`

CUDA-Q surface: Quake, CC, and QEC MLIR dialects, pass manager and pass plugins, decomposition, basis conversion, Clifford+T and angle synthesis, routing, QIR code generation, resource estimation

| Capability | CUDA-Q baseline | Status | Priority | Dependency class | FlagQuantum maturity | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mlir_dialect_stack` | Quake, CC, and QEC dialects on MLIR with a full pass pipeline | unsupported | later | B_open_neutral | `ir` | FlagQuantum IR is a JSON instruction table. MLIR is Apache-2.0 licensed and vendor-neutral, so adopting it is a build decision rather than a dependency conflict. The internal levels come first. |
| `pass_manager_and_pass_plugins` | A pass manager with an out-of-tree pass plugin interface | partial | now | none | `interop_adapter_contract` | The pass and analysis contracts and the CompilerPassExtension protocol are designed, and the ecosystem SDK exposes the extension kind, but no pass manager consumes the protocol and compilation paths remain fixed pipelines. |
| `gate_decomposition_patterns` | Decomposition and DecompositionPatterns libraries expanding operations into a target basis | partial | next | none | `ir` | Native gate legalization exists but there is no rule library, so a target basis outside the legalization table cannot be reached. |
| `basis_conversion` | BasisConversion rewriting a circuit between named gate sets | partial | next | none | `ir` | Partial coverage follows from the legalization table; there is no general conversion between two arbitrary named bases. |
| `clifford_t_synthesis` | Clifford+T synthesis from a rotation angle | unsupported | next | B_open_neutral | none | Absent. The algorithms are published and vendor-neutral, and any implementation needs exact arithmetic that FlagQuantum does not currently carry. |
| `angle_synthesis` | Angle synthesis for a target rotation accuracy | unsupported | next | B_open_neutral | none | Absent, and it shares the exact-arithmetic requirement with Clifford+T synthesis. |
| `topology_aware_routing` | CableRoughIn and topology-aware qubit routing | partial | now | none | `ir` | Routing, topology legalization, and directional topology modules exist as a skeleton, but there is no published-quality router comparable to a SABRE-class algorithm. |
| `commutation_aware_rewrite` | CommutationAwareRewrite pass | partial | next | none | `ir` | The analysis and one rewrite consumer are implemented. `flagquantum/compiler/commutation.py` answers the two questions a reduction needs -- whether two instructions commute, and which instructions form one commuting block on a wire -- and its rule source is a source of proof rather than of record: it reads the two instructions' operator schemas and proves the commutation, with disjoint support unconditional and a gate the rule source has no rule for treated as a barrier. `flagquantum/compiler/commutation_cancellation.py` is the consumer: `cancel_commuting_self_inverse` removes parameter-free, matrix-free members of the self-inverse set in proven pairs, keeping the last member of an odd group so what the block preserves is applied as late as it was before, and it is scheduled inside the pipeline's fixed-point loop, so `cx(0, 1) rz(0) cx(0, 1)` reduces to `rz(0)` where the wire-local self-inverse merge could not see it. What is absent is the part CUDA-Q's row is named for. CUDA-Q's pass is a driver: `CommutationAwareRewriteMatcher` searches backward from an anchor operation for the nearest earlier endpoint that a consumer will accept, crossing a frontier only where pairwise commutation or disjoint support is proven, and the consumer owns the endpoint's algebraic identity. FlagQuantum has one consumer hard-coded against the analysis instead of a matcher a second rewrite can plug into, so no pass can reorder a gate past a commuter to expose a cancellation that a different pass then takes. There is also no per-block analysis invalidation, because there is no pass manager to invalidate through, and no linear-use-def guard, because `CircuitIR` is a straight-line instruction list in which nothing can branch: the same fact that makes the guard unnecessary here is what makes the search unnecessary, which is why the two are one gap rather than two. |
| `dead_code_elimination` | DeadQuantumElimination and general dead code elimination | unsupported | next | none | `ir` | Absent, and the earlier reason this row gave -- that it depends on the pass infrastructure -- does not survive measurement, because the neighbouring commutation row was reconciled without any pass infrastructure at all. CUDA-Q's pass does two things, and neither has a representation here. It removes a `quake.null_wire` whose only use is `quake.sink`, and a `quake.alloca` whose only use is its matching `quake.dealloc` or which has no use at all. `CircuitIR` declares its width once as `n_wires` and the operator schema table holds no allocation, release, null-wire, or sink opcode, so a wire that was never allocated cannot exist and the object this elimination removes is not denotable. What is left is the general half -- a gate whose result no later reader observes -- and that is where the semantics first have to be settled, because the answer differs by output class. `fq.run` returns the whole statevector, so a gate on a wire nothing else touches is observable in the returned state and eliminating it would change the result; a program that declares `measurements` or `observables` has named its outputs, and only there can a wire with no reader be dead. A pass written against one reading would be wrong for the other, and no such declaration of output class is a property of `CircuitIR` today: an empty measurements tuple means both `the caller wants no measurement` and `the state is the answer`. That distinction is the work this row is actually waiting on, and it is recorded rather than implied. |
| `qir_code_generation` | QIR and Profile-QIR code generation to LLVM | partial | now | B_open_neutral | `compiler_qir_emission` | The earlier reason on this row was wrong and is replaced by measurement: FlagQuantum does not emit OpenQASM and QCIS text only. `flagquantum/compiler/qir.py` emits QIR base-profile LLVM IR -- a `FlagQuantumEntryPoint` definition carrying the `entry_point` attribute, `__quantum__qis__*` calls for the lowered program, `__quantum__qis__mz__body` for each measured wire, `__quantum__rt__tuple_record_output` and `__quantum__rt__result_record_output` for the output, the declarations those calls need, and the `qir_major_version`/`qir_minor_version`/`dynamic_qubit_management`/`dynamic_result_management` module flags -- and it is reachable from the public compiler surface, since `translate(program, format="qir-2.0")` is one of the four `TRANSLATION_FORMATS` and `target_emission` carries a `qir-2.0` profile whose emitter is this function. QIR is vendor-neutral, so the whole path is software this programme can own. The reason the row is `partial` rather than `supported` is the half of CUDA-Q's row that is absent: CUDA-Q generates *Profile-QIR*, and this emitter is the base profile only. The adaptive profile is absent, and with both dynamic-management module flags `false` so are `__quantum__rt__qubit_allocate_array`, `__quantum__rt__qubit_release_array`, and every `read_result` call, which is the same gap the runtime qubit allocation row records from the IR side. Pulse-level generation and runtime library extension calls are absent, only the constant-index pointer kind is emitted, and there is no LLVM compilation to an object file or an executable: this is text, and no external QIR validator was run against it, so conformance is the repository's own semantic check plus a host C parser accepting the text as LLVM IR syntax. An opcode with no QIS instruction is lowered to a native sequence equal to the requested gate up to an unconditional global phase the base profile cannot express, and a gate the profile cannot carry is refused by index and opcode rather than approximated. |
| `target_text_emitters` | OpenQASM and vendor JSON emitters | partial | next | none | `ir` | An OpenQASM emitter exists. The emitter set is narrower than the CUDA-Q roster. |
| `resource_estimation` | estimate_resources reporting gate counts, depth, width, and qubit peak | partial | next | none | `compiler_resource_estimation` | The static half exists. `flagquantum/compiler/resource_estimation.py` reports the operation count per opcode, the schedule depth, the per-wire depth, the widest operation, the T family and its depth, the channel count, and the declared register width, over the instruction sequence the caller wrote, with the basis named in the record as `static_instruction_sequence`. It refuses a program whose sequence has data dependence, naming the instruction index, and that refusal is what the row now turns on: a straight-line list has no loop bound, so loops and functions stay unestimatable until ProgramIR exists, exactly as this row recorded before any of the rest was built. The estimate is also not a latency and not a device cost -- no gate duration, connectivity, or routing overhead enters it -- and no basis conversion runs, so the counts are of the opcodes the caller wrote rather than of a lowered basis. Qubit peak is not a separate field; the register width and the used wires are. The fault-tolerant layer above the tally landed separately, as `flagquantum.algorithms.logical_resources` charging the tally on a rotated surface code. |
| `compiler_plugin_ecosystem` | Third-party compiler passes distributed out of tree | partial | now | none | `extension_sdk` | The extension protocol and lifecycle exist, but no discovery path reaches compilation, so an out-of-tree pass cannot run. |
| `foreign_circuit_import` | from_qasm and from_qiskit bringing a foreign circuit into the framework | partial | next | none | `qiskit_interop` | The Qiskit direction exists: an ecosystem adapter builds a FlagQuantum circuit from a provider object. OpenQASM import does not, and the OpenQASM surface FlagQuantum carries is an emitter, so a circuit that exists only as text cannot enter the framework. |

#### Noise and error models

Domain id: `noise_and_error_models`

CUDA-Q surface: Kraus channels, noise model callbacks, trajectory simulation, density matrix, Pauli tracking, detector error models, unitary-mixture degradation

| Capability | CUDA-Q baseline | Status | Priority | Dependency class | FlagQuantum maturity | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kraus_channel_algebra` | Kraus channels and general noise channels | partial | now | none | `noisy_simulation` | A general Kraus constructor exists and is validated. `KrausChannel` accepts an arbitrary operator list, refuses a set that is not trace-preserving (completeness compared at `atol = rtol = 1e-6`) and a dimension that is not a positive power of two, serializes through the `flagquantum.kraus_channel.v1` schema, and reaches simulation through `NoiseModel.add` and `Circuit.noisy_density_matrix`. What is absent is the operator type the CUDA-Q surface builds a channel from: no matrix-valued operator participates in operator algebra, which is the gap `matrix_and_custom_operator` already records. |
| `noise_model_callback` | Noise model callbacks injecting noise by operation type at runtime | partial | next | none | `noisy_simulation` | Per-gate (`NoiseModel.add(gate_names, channel)`) and per-qubit (`wires=`) static injection both exist, and lowering now refuses a rule that cannot apply. The callback form is absent, and `NoiseRule` carries a `KrausChannel` fixed at construction. A callback cannot be added to `NoiseRule` as it stands: `NoiseModel.identity` is a SHA-256 digest of `to_dict()`, and checkpoint resume and execution-plan identity both bind to it, so a channel chosen by an arbitrary callable would make identity unreproducible. Any such rule must be registered under a declared name and parameterization before it can participate in a model identity. |
| `batched_trajectory` | Batched trajectory execution | partial | next | none | `noisy_simulation` | Trajectory simulation exists; batched execution across trajectories is narrower than the baseline. |
| `detector_error_model` | Detector error model construction and circuit-to-DEM conversion | partial | now | B_open_neutral | `detector_error_model` | Both directions of the stim text interchange work. `from_memory_circuit` builds a model exactly for Pauli noise over the reference Clifford gate set; `to_stim_text` emits text stim 1.16.0 parses; `from_stim_text` reads everything stim wrote in a 240-model developer-time sweep except a `repeat` block, and `str(model.flattened())` is a complete route around that one refusal; both readings of a `^` separator are offered under upstream's own `use_decomp_suggestions` flag name, and the default is the one stim itself means, measured against stim's own sampler rather than asserted. The model can also state that mechanisms are alternatives rather than independent, which is the one thing its parity matrices cannot carry: an error id groups them, the marginal rates and the sampler read a group as one fault, and the text writer refuses an id-carrying model instead of printing an independent one under the same probabilities. The row stays partial because conversion is narrower than the baseline at the input end: `from_memory_circuit` accepts one circuit record and one noise record, so an arbitrary circuit carrying detector and observable annotations has no route to a model, and a non-Pauli channel is refused rather than decomposed. `flagquantum/qec/IMPLEMENTATION.md` records the sweeps and the arithmetic. |
| `unitary_mixture_degradation` | Unitary-mixture noise models distinguished from general channels | partial | next | none | `noisy_simulation` | The distinction is made in the noise layer and is decided by the operators rather than by the channel's name: `KrausChannel.unitary_mixture` reports the branches and their weights, and the criterion is that every operator is a non-negative real scale times a unitary, with the whole Gram matrix checked rather than its leading entry, so an amplitude damping channel is refused for its unequal singular values. A zero-weight operator is a branch of probability zero and is dropped rather than read as a general channel, so every built-in factory stays classified at the edges of its range. One consumer reads the answer: the stabilizer positioned-noise entry point executes a one- or two-wire channel whose branches are Pauli frames and refuses every other channel by name, so a depolarizing channel samples as its four frames where it previously refused. Two limits keep the row partial. The framework comparison gives no Python accessor for the property at all, so there is no external surface to conform against and the contract here is FlagQuantum's own. And only one consumer reads it: the density-matrix and trajectory routes execute a general channel without asking whether it is a mixture, so the sampling advantage a mixture allows is unrealised there. |
