| `spin_operator_algebra` | SpinOperator and Pauli operator algebra | partial | now | none | `ir` | Pauli observables exist. Operator arithmetics for products, sums, scalars, exponentials, commutators, and anticommutators are absent. |
| `fermion_operator_algebra` | FermionOperator with Jordan-Wigner and related mappings | partial | next | none | `observables_fermion_operator_algebra` | The algebra and one mapping exist. `flagquantum/observables/fermion.py` builds a normal-ordered sum over spin orbitals with `create`, `annihilate`, and `number`; addition, subtraction, unary negation, scalar multiplication, `*`, `dagger`, `commutator`, and `anticommutator` are all present, so a chemistry workload's generator is an expression rather than a hand-applied relation, and equality is structural, which makes `is_hermitian` exact rather than a tolerance test. `jordan_wigner` maps a Hermitian operator to the Pauli `Observable` the existing statevector path already measures, which is how a fermionic observable acquires a value. What is absent is the rest of the mapping family this row's own wording names: Bravyi-Kitaev, parity, and ternary-tree encodings do not exist, and neither does any reduction in the Pauli weight of the image, which is the reason those encodings exist at all. The mode count is an argument rather than inferred, and no matrix form of a fermionic operator ships. |
| `boson_operator_algebra` | BosonOperator algebra | partial | later | none | `observables_boson_operator_algebra` | The algebra exists. `flagquantum/observables/boson.py` builds normal-ordered operators over modes of unbounded occupation in the Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt basis, with `create`, `annihilate`, `number`, `position`, `momentum`, and `identity`, the same arithmetic surface as the fermionic algebra, and `to_matrix` evaluates one as a dense matrix over a Fock space whose truncation dimension the caller names, refused above a byte ceiling. The row stays partial because the algebra still has no consumer and no execution path: there is no bosonic or photonic backend, no Fock-space state, no expectation value, and no qubit mapping for a bosonic operator, so the dense form is a reference and a test oracle rather than a production route. The truncation dimension is the caller's because the commutation relations live on untruncated monomials -- the commutator of two truncated ladder matrices differs from the identity at the top level -- and only the explicit dimension says which operator a caller's numbers describe. |
| `super_operator_algebra` | SuperOperator for superoperator representations | partial | now | none | `continuous_time_lindblad` | The algebra is implemented: `flagquantum/operators/superoperator.py` states a superoperator as a sum of `coefficient * left @ state @ right` terms, where a missing side is a one-sided multiplication, with the three CUDA-Q constructors and an accumulating `+=`; `apply` and `dense` are two independent formulas in the repository-wide row-major vectorization `vec(A rho B) = (A (x) B^T) vec(rho)`, and the Lindblad generator assembled that way is the same arithmetic as `Liouvillian.dense()`, so the check that used to read 4.441e-16 now reads exactly 0.0. What is absent is everything beyond construction and the two views: no Choi, PTM, or Kraus representation transform, no partial trace, and no adjoint on the algebra. The factor contract has two implementations, `torch.Tensor` and `PauliSum`, both supplying `__matmul__`, `__rmatmul__` and `dense()`, so a matrix-free Hamiltonian enters a term without being materialized. The row stays partial rather than supported because CUDA-Q's row is about superoperator representations and this is the construction-and-evaluation half. |
| `matrix_and_custom_operator` | MatrixOperator and custom_op | partial | next | none | none | A stable operator schema and discovery interface exist, and a matrix can now enter the superoperator algebra as a term factor. What is still missing is a matrix-valued operator type in the operator algebra itself: no `MatrixOperator` or `custom_op` type composes with `Observable` or the fermionic sum through products, sums, scalars, adjoints, or commutators, and the superoperator factor contract is deliberately narrower than that, requiring only `__matmul__`, `__rmatmul__` and `dense()`. |
| `exponential_pauli_operator` | exp_pauli and pauli_word construction | partial | next | none | none | The dense constructor exists: `flagquantum/simulation/pauli.py` reads a Pauli word and its targets positionally, so character `i` of the word acts on `targets[i]`, and returns the operator the pair denotes on a declared number of wires. A Pauli product squares to the identity, so the exponential is evaluated in closed form as `exp(-i theta P) = cos(theta) I - i sin(theta) P` rather than by exponentiating a matrix; the form is exact at every angle and is checked against an eigendecomposition of the product and against the defining series of the exponential. An `I` character consumes its target and contributes no support, so a word aligns with a wire list without dropping the wires it does not act on, and an all-identity word returns the global phase it denotes instead of the identity. A word whose length disagrees with the number of targets, a character outside `X`, `Y`, `Z` and `I`, a repeated target, a target outside the declared wires, and a non-finite angle are each refused. What is absent is the circuit-level form, and it is the whole of the row: no operation the IR carries and no compiler pattern decomposes it into single-qubit basis changes and a CNOT chain, so a circuit cannot contain an exponential of a Pauli product, no rotation parameter reaches it as a differentiable value, and `pauli_word` is not a value type a kernel parameter can be written with. The dense constructor is the operator those three would be built from. |
| `chemistry_domain_library` | PySCF driver, UCCSD, and hardware-efficient ansatz libraries | partial | now | B_open_neutral | `algorithms_chemistry_ansatz` | The ansatz half exists and the integrals half does not. `flagquantum/algorithms/chemistry.py` enumerates the single and double excitations of an electron count in a spin-orbital count, builds the fermionic generator of one, emits the exact circuit that realizes its exponential, composes them into the UCCSD circuit, and covers a hardware-efficient and a coupler hardware-efficient ansatz with a parameter count; the gate sequences are the ones CUDA-Q's own kernels apply, so a workload built around them transfers. What is absent is the first entry point this row names: there is no PySCF or other driver dependency, so no molecular Hamiltonian, no basis set, no active space, no Hartree-Fock solve, and no energy reference arrives from here. Two divergences from the baseline are deliberate and stated rather than silent: an occupied index above a virtual one is refused instead of emitting an empty ladder that would be a local rotation rather than an excitation, and `uccsd_excitations` fills the lowest n_electrons spin orbitals where CUDA-Q's `get_uccsd_excitations` divides by two before rounding up, so the two agree on even electron counts only. |
| `rydberg_analog_hamiltonian` | RydbergHamiltonian for analog neutral-atom evolution | unsupported | later | none | none | Absent. It is the observable-side input an analog neutral-atom target would need, so it follows that target rather than preceding it. |

Trotter time evolution landed as flagquantum.algorithms.trotter: a weighted Pauli sum becomes an ordinary Circuit through a product formula of order 1 or 2, with the exact circuit for one Pauli word's exponential as its primitive. Block encoding landed next as flagquantum.algorithms.primitives.block_encoding, promoted out of the private helper flagquantum.algorithms.svd held, and it carries the qubitization walk step with it: the reflection is emitted as one dense matrix, the flagged block is the matrix over the caller's subnormalisation, and one walk step is a rotation whose eigenphases are the arccosines of the encoded eigenvalues. The fermion-qubit transform family already had jordan_wigner at flagquantum.observables.fermion. Still absent: qubitization as a public walk object carrying a moment count, the Pauli linear-combination encoding, QSVT, double factorization, and the Bravyi-Kitaev, parity and ternary-tree transforms. The plan's original route -- adapt Qualtran, Apache-2.0, which covers the same mathematics -- was ruled out by the repository owner: Qualtran 0.7.0 carries 27 transitive dependencies and is not declared in dependency-policy.toml, so the mathematics is implemented natively instead and no third-party quantum-algorithm library is a dependency. |
| `error_mitigation` | Zero-noise extrapolation, probabilistic error cancellation, and Clifford data regression | partial | now | none | `algorithms_zero_noise_extrapolation` | Zero-noise extrapolation and probabilistic error cancellation, not Clifford data regression. An observable is measured at several error strengths by scaling the one error-probability parameter each noise channel declares, and the curve is continued to zero by polynomial least squares or Richardson extrapolation, which reports the residual it left and the variance amplification of its weights. The channel families whose parameters are not error probabilities are refused by name, and a model that declares a readout rule is refused rather than measured without it, because the estimate is Tr(O rho) and classical readout confusion is applied after measurement. Beside that, a channel the model declares as a Pauli channel is inverted exactly by decomposing its inverse into a signed combination of Pauli words read off its Pauli transfer matrix, one location at a time, which reports the sampling overhead gamma squared that a sampled implementation would pay and refuses by measured magnitude the channel families whose transfer matrix is not diagonal and the channels whose transfer eigenvalue reaches zero. Readout-error mitigation and Clifford data regression are absent. |

Gradient correctness under sharding is registered separately and is not asserted here. |

SPSA is implemented as a standalone optimizer that consumes a plain objective callable and a parameter tensor instead of a gradient, and it spends two objective evaluations per step whatever the parameter count, which is the same recursion cudaq.optimizers exposes; the parity entry records its boundary rather than a convergence claim, and the estimator is biased rather than a gradient. COBYLA and NelderMead are still absent, and the training entry point still refuses an optimizer that is not a PyTorch one, so an SPSA run is a caller-owned loop and not an fq.train call. |

#### Quantum error correction

Domain id: `quantum_error_correction`

CUDA-Q surface: cudaq-qec library, detector, detectors, and logical_observable annotations in a kernel, dem, dem_from_kernel, and DEMResult, extract_syndrome, circuit-to-DEM round trip, Stim integration, the logical.* preview namespace, QEC MLIR dialect, GPU decoders, surface, Steane, and qLDPC codes, lattice surgery and magic state distillation, transport, rounds, objectives, neutral atoms, for-stim-users migration

| Capability | CUDA-Q baseline | Status | Priority | Dependency class | FlagQuantum maturity | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qec_code_library` | cudaq-qec codes expressed as kernels, with numerical experiment APIs | partial | now | none | `stabilizer_code_memory_circuit` | The repetition code, the rotated surface code and the Steane code are declared as code records and each produces a memory-experiment source with detector and observable layouts, so a distance-d rotated patch is expressible and a code carrying both a Z-type and an X-type readout is expressible through Steane. A code record can now also be read into matrices rather than only into a circuit: css_code_matrices lifts its four blocks into a CssCodeMatrices record, which carries hz, hx, lz and lx together, so a code whose stabilizers are known reaches a code-capacity detector error model on either readout basis without a gadget being built for it and without losing a fault family. The families remain declared rather than constructed, and an arbitrary parity-check matrix still has no route in: a check states one ancilla and one CNOT direction fixed by its type, so a mixed X-and-Z stabilizer is refused, and a logical observable that is neither pure X nor pure Z is refused rather than half-read, so qLDPC, Reichardt and Floquet codes are absent and a colour code has no record even though the CSS shape now admits one. The code records themselves still expose no decode entry point, because decoding belongs to the decoder row and reads a detector error model rather than a code. The noise record states a rate per fault family and the same rate per element, so a per-location profile is expressible: the four scalars and their per-qubit and per-check overrides are PhenomenologicalNoise's, read against the code's own vectors. |
| `qec_decoder_family` | Minimum-weight perfect matching, belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding, and sliding-window decoders | partial | now | B_open_neutral | `detector_error_matching_decoder` | Matching is now self-implemented rather than absent: the detector error model becomes a weighted decoding graph whose edge weight is log((1 - p) / p), and a syndrome is decoded exactly by enumerating the ways to pair its defective detectors and to route any of them to the graph's boundary. The row stays partial on scope, not on correctness. Matching needs a graphlike model and refuses a hyperedge rather than projecting it onto a pair, so a code whose mechanisms flip three or more detectors is outside this row's matching half. The pairing is enumerated, so a syndrome is bounded by a defect budget instead of decoded at scale. Belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding is absent, so the LDPC codes the baseline serves with it are not served here; the sliding-window decoder for a long-lived experiment is absent; and there is no decoder registry or plugin protocol, so a decoder is constructed directly rather than requested by name. The baseline's GPU decoders are deliberately not chased, because the CUDA-Q qLDPC decoder is a closed-source shared library, so only its interface position is a target and an Apache-2.0 implementation is the route if that scope is ever reached. The row fails closed on a second gap of its own: because the graph keeps one edge per mechanism, a model that states one detector-and-observable signature twice would become two parallel edges and the matcher would take the cheaper, so the decoder requires a unique signature before it weights anything and refuses a duplicate with the merge that resolves it named in the refusal. It fails closed on the neighbouring statement for the neighbouring reason: a model that says two mechanisms are alternatives is refused and the groups are named, because one weight per mechanism is the weight of a fault that fires alone while a group of alternatives is one fault whose weight is the negative log-likelihood of the group, so weighting the members separately would charge the model more than the fault costs. The cross-check half has landed and it is a comparison of two selections rather than an equality of two instruments: PyMatching is behind the `pymatching` extra and is never the authority, and because its own accumulator reports 3.9020747171643912 for a mechanism this row states as 3.9020746947749574 the graph it minimizes over is not exactly this one. The row therefore asserts the cheapest weight on every syndrome, the observables wherever the cheapest explanation is unique, and the two refusals as the same set, with a pinned tie on the distance-three repetition code so the tie clause is demonstrated. The registry, the two decoder families the matcher does not cover, and the hyperedge front end were the work this row still named; of those, the registry has landed and is described above. A decoder registry has since landed, and it is the factory half of the baseline's decoder surface rather than the whole of it: flagquantum.qec.get_decoder(name, source, **options) reaches a decoder by name and flagquantum.qec.register_decoder(name, *, replace=False) puts one there, with registration checked while the registering module is imported so a class missing decode or from_detector_error_model is refused there rather than at the first caller. The registry is deliberately narrower than upstream's. Its source argument takes the three carriers a caller can hold a model in -- the detector error model, stim's text for one, and the decoding graph the model defines -- and not H_or_dem_text_or_sparse_matrix, because lifting a parity-check matrix would also mean choosing the noise model and round count that from_code_matrices reads rather than defaults. It holds the detector-error-model family alone, because the repetition-code decoders here take an ordered syndrome history rather than detection events and one name space over two input protocols would make a name mean one of two things. It fails closed rather than falling back: an unregistered name raises and lists the registered names, a source that is not one of the three carriers is refused by type, and no name is preferred over another, so the authority is returned for its own name wherever the optional extra happens to be installed. The remaining work inside this row is therefore the two decoder families the matcher does not cover, the hyperedge front end, and the plugin boundary the baseline ships -- the registered adapter is a concrete class under a name rather than a plugin loaded across a version boundary. |
| `qec_stim_integration` | Stim sampling and detector error model interoperability | partial | now | B_open_neutral | `stabilizer_sampling`, `detector_error_model`, `qec_memory_circuit_sampling` | All three halves now exist, and the row is partial on scope rather than on connection. Stim-backed sampling landed with the stabilizer engine, the detector error model half landed with the text reader and its own capability entry, and the join landed last: a memory circuit is lowered once, each configured noise location is placed at the instruction it belongs to, the result is executed on the stabilizer engine, and the detection events and observable flips are read off the recorded bits. A decoder built from that same circuit's model then decodes those events, so a logical-failure rate no longer needs the statevector ceiling that bounds construction. What the row still lacks is breadth of the noise grammar: a location is a data flip at a round boundary or a measurement flip at a check's readout, which is what the phenomenological record names, while a channel placed after an arbitrary gate has no location and is still declined. The x_ and z_ variants are absent for the same reason the code record is a Z-memory record. Decoding itself stays with the decoder row rather than being implied here. The row names three registry entries because the implementation genuinely spans three: the sampling half is `stabilizer_sampling`, the interchange half is `detector_error_model`, and the join that consumes both is `qec_memory_circuit_sampling`. The row is read only against cudaq-qec, which is where the detector error models live; where the two components divide this surface is recorded in `baseline.surface_ownership`. <br><br>Narrower scope at this status: No sampling of error-corrected logical operations, and no noise grammar wider than the phenomenological record. A channel placed after a named gate, an x_ or z_ variant over a state preparation, and pymatching- or stim-driven logical-error-rate estimation all remain absent, so a circuit whose noise is neither a round-boundary data flip nor a readout flip is declined rather than sampled. |

| `qec_logical_operations` | Lattice surgery, product rotation, and magic state distillation | partial | later | B_open_neutral | `stabilizer_code_memory_circuit` | Readout-basis half only. Of those three, product rotation is present: `certify_logical_product` checks a candidate single-patch Pauli product against the code's own checks and its same-type stabilizer span, and `derive_anticommuting_logical_product` solves the code's opposite-type checks over GF(2) for the partner of a declared observable, so one code record is read out in either Pauli basis and the detector error model of a rotated frame carries observable-live mechanisms that the default frame does not. So the document cannot be translated from that page, and reading the row's name as pointing at it would aim a `next`-priority capability at a component that produces no detector error model. The document is conformance work rather than a new implementation, so it is still sequenced after the Stim integration row's halves are joined; until then a migration guide would describe a route that stops at the join. |

#### Logical and fault-tolerant layer

Domain id: `logical_and_ftqc_layer`

CUDA-Q surface: preview/logical, logical resource estimation, Gidney-Ekera adder, carbon code, Fermi-Hubbard, distillation factories, gadget verification, physical placement, schedule, and routing, Stim output, device and constraint modeling

| Capability | CUDA-Q baseline | Status | Priority | Dependency class | FlagQuantum maturity | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `logical_resource_estimation` | Clifford+T and surface-code area and time estimation for a logical algorithm | partial | next | B_open_neutral | `algorithms_logical_resource_estimation` | A rotated-surface-code cost over the compiler's own static estimate rather than a second tally: flagquantum.algorithms.logical_resources reads the operation counts, the T family, and the schedule depth from flagquantum.compiler.resource_estimation.estimate_resources and adds the code layer, at a distance the caller names, as 2 d^2 - 1 physical qubits per patch and d surface-code cycles per logical layer. The row is partial for three named reasons. The input has to already be Clifford+T: a parametric rotation is refused rather than synthesised, because angle synthesis is absent and a T-count taken over an un-synthesised angle would be the count of a circuit nobody will run, and a compound operation whose T-count is its decomposition's -- a Toffoli, a controlled swap -- is refused, because a Toffoli is not a Clifford gate and the decompositions do not agree on what it costs. There is no distillation factory, magic-state budget, routing overhead, placement, scheduling, or device model, so the physical figure is a floor for a circuit of these layers rather than a compiled estimate. And no logical error rate is reported, because a threshold fit's prefactor and threshold are a device's numbers rather than this unit's. Clifford+T synthesis, angle synthesis, and the arithmetic constructions are the moves that would take this row to supported. |
| `arithmetic_bloqs` | Gidney-Ekera adder and related arithmetic constructions | unsupported | later | B_open_neutral | none | Absent. The Gidney-Ekera construction is a Clifford+T circuit, so once it is written it can be costed by the logical_resource_estimation unit that now exists, but writing the adder is an implementation of its own and no arithmetic construction exists here. The Qualtran adaptation that was the planned route to both rows is not the route that was taken: the logical estimator reuses the in-repository compiler estimate instead, and it carries no Qualtran dependency for an adder to reuse. |
| `physical_placement_and_scheduling` | Physical qubit placement, schedule, and routing for a logical architecture | unsupported | later | none | none | Absent. It also depends on a physical target model, so it follows the compiler routing work. |
| `ftqc_device_modeling` | Device and constraint modeling for a fault-tolerant architecture | unsupported | later | none | none | Absent. It is a modeling surface with no consumer until logical resource estimation exists. |
| `logical_gadget_verification` | Gadget verification and distillation factory validation | unsupported | later | none | none | Absent, and it depends on both the logical layer and the QEC decoders. |

#### Realtime control

Domain id: `realtime_control`

CUDA-Q surface: FPGA-to-GPU microsecond feedback, NVQLink network layer, Holoscan sensor bridge, RoCE and Ethernet transport, device call channels, host API, messaging protocol

| Capability | CUDA-Q baseline | Status | Priority | Dependency class | FlagQuantum maturity | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `realtime_feedback_loop` | Microsecond-scale FPGA-to-GPU feedback loop | unsupported | next | A_nvidia_proprietary | none | Blocked, not merely absent. The software half of the surface now exists in flagquantum/remote/realtime, but the microsecond feedback loop itself needs an FPGA and a remote-direct-memory-access capable network interface, so it cannot be closed by software at all and is delivered, if at all, with a hardware partner. ARCH-013 records it as an owned blocked row rather than as a plan. |
| `realtime_transport` | RoCE and Ethernet realtime transport with a device call channel | unsupported | next | A_nvidia_proprietary | none | Partly closed and still not a transport. The vendor-neutral messaging protocol and the device-call channel seam a transport plugs into now exist in flagquantum/remote/realtime, with the slot framing, payload type system, status convention, and function table specified and exercised offline. What remains absent is the transport itself: RoCE and Ethernet carriage, a ring buffer, a dispatcher, and every timing property, none of which software alone can supply. The row stays unsupported so the dependency-class accounting is not flattered by a protocol that measures nothing. |
| `realtime_host_api` | Host API and messaging protocol for realtime control | partial | next | B_open_neutral | `realtime_device_call_messaging` | Partly delivered. The vendor-neutral half is the messaging protocol and the device-call abstraction, and both are now implemented and conformance-checked offline in flagquantum/remote/realtime: a fixed-size slot, a typed payload declared by a handler schema, a function table keyed by a hashed handler name, a status convention, and a channel resolved by name at runtime. What keeps the row at partial rather than supported is the other half of the host-facing surface: the dispatcher, the ring buffer, the function-table launch path, and the occupancy and graph entry points are absent by design, because they belong to the hardware partner and to a device runtime this repository does not own. |
| `realtime_sensor_bridge` | Holoscan sensor bridge integration | unsupported | later | A_nvidia_proprietary | none | Absent and NVIDIA-specific. A FlagOS-family equivalent is the replacement target, and it follows the protocol definition; the protocol now exists, while the sensor bridge and its transport do not, so nothing about this row is closed. |
